generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, this connected view is how you make sense of any study you meet, from a coaching trial to a paper on training loads. You look for the research question, see how the study was designed and limited, and follow the method, results and discussion through to what was found. Held together, the three strands turn a technical sport study into something you can follow.
generatedProse.worked-example: Tom and Amara both read the same study on a new warm-up routine. Tom jumps to the results, notes that it worked, and cannot say what the study was really testing. Amara finds the research question first, sees how the athletes and the trial were chosen and limited, and follows the method, results and discussion through to the findings. Reading the study as one connected whole, Amara can judge what it showed; Tom only has a number.
generatedProse.summary: Research in sport makes most sense when you see it as one connected whole. A research question becomes a designed study, and that study takes a recognisable shape on the page, carrying it from question to findings. It is this connected view, not any single part on its own, that helps you read sport research across your course.

check.body: A student reads a journal article. They spot the focused question in the introduction, notice how the study was shaped and limited, and follow the method, results and discussion through to the findings. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That they are reading research as one connected whole, using the three strands together to follow it from question to findings.
_items.feedback: Yes. The three strands worked together as one view of the whole project.

_items.text: That the article was too simple to count as real research.
_items.feedback: Spotting the parts does not make the research simple; it shows the strands working together.

_items.text: That only the introduction matters when you read research.
_items.feedback: Each part did a job here, not just the introduction.

_items.text: That the student was only interested in the final results.
_items.feedback: They followed the whole thread, from the question through to the findings.
